headline_marked: Over 50 [[garment workers fall ill suddenly]] at Savar factory
headline: Over 50 garment workers fall ill suddenly at Savar factory
summary: Workers at Magpie Composite Textile Ltd reported breathing difficulties and dizziness, with similar incidents reported across other Ashulia factories.
details: Nearly 50 garment workers at Magpie Composite Textile Ltd in Ashulia, Savar, fell ill over two days, requiring urgent medical treatment at local hospitals.

Affected workers reported experiencing sudden shortness of breath, dizziness, and nausea. Some claimed they felt ill immediately after smelling a strange odor or feeling hot air while handling fabric in the sewing section.
On Tuesday morning, 20-25 workers were rushed to hospitals via factory vehicles and auto-rickshaws. A similar incident occurred on Monday afternoon where 10-12 workers were treated.
Medical staff at Savar Labzone Hospital confirmed that approximately 20 patients arrived with respiratory issues and dizziness, most of whom are now stable.
Factory management estimated the number of affected workers to be between 25-30, while some workers claimed they had not eaten breakfast, suggesting varying accounts of the cause.

Ashulia Industrial Area Police-1 officials stated that several workers from multiple factories in the area have reported similar symptoms over the last four days, though the exact cause remains unknown.
As a precautionary measure, another factory named Lusaka has reportedly granted leave to its workers following similar health concerns.
caption:
Over 50 garment workers in Savar suddenly fell ill with breathing difficulties and dizziness. What caused the sudden collapse?

Nearly 50 garment workers at Magpie Composite Textile Ltd in Ashulia, Savar, fell ill over two days, requiring urgent medical treatment at local hospitals.

Affected workers reported experiencing sudden shortness of breath, dizziness, and nausea. Some claimed they felt ill immediately after smelling a strange odor or feeling hot air while handling fabric in the sewing section.

On Tuesday morning, 20-25 workers were rushed to hospitals via factory vehicles and auto-rickshaws. A similar incident occurred on Monday afternoon where 10-12 workers were treated.

Medical staff at Savar Labzone Hospital confirmed that approximately 20 patients arrived with respiratory issues and dizziness, most of whom are now stable.

Factory management estimated the number of affected workers to be between 25-30, while some workers claimed they had not eaten breakfast, suggesting varying accounts of the cause.

Ashulia Industrial Area Police-1 officials stated that several workers from multiple factories in the area have reported similar symptoms over the last four days, though the exact cause remains unknown.

As a precautionary measure, another factory named Lusaka has reportedly granted leave to its workers following similar health concerns.

headline_marked: 4 youth lured to Teknaf, [[4 youth rescued from mountain hideout]]
headline: 4 youth lured to Teknaf, 4 youth rescued from mountain hideout
summary: The young men from Feni and Habiganj were kidnapped after being promised high-paying jobs; kidnappers demanded 1 million BDT ransom.
details: Four young men from Feni and Habiganj were rescued by a joint operation of RAB and police on Tuesday afternoon from a mountain hideout in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar.
The victims, aged 19 to 23, were lured to Teknaf on June 27 with the promise of high-paying jobs. They were then held captive for three days in a mountain shelter.
According to the Teknaf Model Police Station, the kidnappers demanded a ransom of 1 million BDT from the families of the victims, threatening to kill them if the payment was not made.
One family had reportedly paid 50,000 BDT as part of the ransom. The victims' families reported that the kidnappers used phone calls to demand money and threatened the victims.
A joint operation was conducted in the Rangikhali Jummapara mountain area of Hnila Union, Hnila Union, Teknaf, between 12:00 PM and 2:30 PM on Tuesday.
Despite the rescue, the kidnappers, including a man named Russell, were unable to be arrested as they fled into the jungle when they police and RAB arrived.
The victims are currently being processed for handover to their families. Police are preparing to be file a case and arrest the kidnappers.
The victims include Imam Hussein (19), Zisan (23), and Tauhidul Islam (19) from Feni, and Sumon Mia alias Hossein (22) from Habiganj.
caption:
Lured by the promise of high-paying jobs, four youth were kidnapped and held in a mountain hideout in Teknaf.

Four young men from Feni and Habiganj were rescued by a joint operation of RAB and police on Tuesday afternoon from a mountain hideout in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar.

The victims, aged 19 to 23, were lured to Teknaf on June 27 with the promise of high-paying jobs. They were then held captive for three days in a mountain shelter.

According to the Teknaf Model Police Station, the kidnappers demanded a ransom of 1 million BDT from the families of the victims, threatening to kill them if the payment was not made.

One family had reportedly paid 50,000 BDT as part of the ransom. The victims' families reported that the kidnappers used phone calls to demand money and threatened the victims.

A joint operation was conducted in the Rangikhali Jummapara mountain area of Hnila Union, Hnila Union, Teknaf, between 12:00 PM and 2:30 PM on Tuesday.

Despite the rescue, the kidnappers, including a man named Russell, were unable to be arrested as they fled into the jungle when they police and RAB arrived.

The victims are currently being processed for handover to their families. Police are preparing to be file a case and arrest the kidnappers.

The victims include Imam Hussein (19), Zisan (23), and Tauhidul Islam (19) from Feni, and Sumon Mia alias Hossein (22) from Habiganj.
